title: Bug Hunt Station 4 - Loot Shop (wrong answers)
body:
Goal: find three bugs that do not crash - the program just gives the wrong answer.

  1. Work out on paper: for the basket [12, 5, 30], what is the total? What is the cheapest item? Can you buy it all with 50 coins?
  2. Open starter.py and press Run. Compare with your paper answers.
  3. Rubber duck time: explain total_price() line by line to your partner (or a toy). Say what each line does each time round the loop.
  4. Fix one bug at a time, and run after each fix.

Done looks like:

Total: 47 coins
Cheapest item: 5 coins
With 50 coins you can buy everything!

Hint for bug 3: if a function only prints, what does it give back?

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run it and compare the output with your paper answers. Each of the three functions has one bug, so check them one at a time. Start with total_price(): is it adding all three prices?

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Add print() lines inside the loop to see what happens each round. Read each function out loud, line by line. Ask: does the loop finish before the function hands back its answer? Does return give back the right variable?

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Look at how far the return is indented in total_price(), because the indent decides when it runs. In cheapest(), check which value is handed back after the loop. In can_buy(), ask what the if line in the program receives.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.html: # Bug Hunt Station 4: Loot Shop # No red errors here - but the answers are WRONG. These are the sneakiest bugs! # There are THREE bugs, one in each function. Work out the right answers on # paper first, then use print() to see where the program goes wrong. def total_price(prices): """Return all the prices added together.""" total = 0 for price in prices: total = total + price return total def cheapest(prices): """Return the smallest price.""" smallest = prices[0] for price in prices: if price < smallest: smallest = price return prices[0] def can_buy(coins, prices): """Return True if the coins are enough to buy everything.""" print(coins >= total_price(prices)) if __name__ == "__main__": basket = [12, 5, 30] print(f"Total: {total_price(basket)} coins") print(f"Cheapest item: {cheapest(basket)} coins") if can_buy(50, basket): print("With 50 coins you can buy everything!") else: print("With 50 coins you cannot buy everything.")
